teams.heading: Maika Sivo is omitted from Mick Potter's Fiji league World Cup squad
teams.body: Fiji league head coach Mick Potter has named his 23-man squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup, with Leeds Rhinos winger Maika Sivo a major omission. Sivo, the Super League's top try-scorer in 2026, missed the club's run-in with arm and shoulder injuries, though his exclusion is not yet confirmed as injury-related. The squad features Super League players Semi Valemei, Waqa Blake, Taane Milne and new Warrington signing Mitchell Prest. The Bati face Cook Islands, Australia and New Zealand in Pool A.

lead.why: It is a highly notable squad announcement for the upcoming tournament, featuring a major star omission.

teams.heading: RFU set to offer England head coach Steve Borthwick contract extension
teams.body: The RFU is set to offer England head coach Steve Borthwick a contract extension that will secure his position beyond next year's World Cup. While Borthwick's tenure has faced scrutiny for being full of tactical contradictions, the union is moving to finalise a deal that offers stability. Former England international Ben Kay insisted Borthwick’s side can reach the standard required to win the tournament, provided the head coach addresses key areas including midfield selection and club relationships ahead of the upcoming autumn campaign.

teams.heading: France amass over 400 points across their last 11 test matches
teams.body: France have scored 426 points and conceded 291 across their last 11 internationals. This sequence yields an average of 38.7 points scored and 26.5 points conceded per match. The largest margin of victory in this 11-match window was a 54-12 away win against Wales in February 2026 during the Six Nations. Currently, France sit third of 12 teams in the Nations Championship table with two victories from their three matches.

teams.heading: Leinster welcome back Jamison Gibson-Park as Harry Byrne faces further assessment
teams.body: Leinster have received a significant boost with Ireland scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park returning to full training, though the club remain without Harry Byrne and Max Deegan. Gibson-Park is available for Saturday's Cardiff clash after recovering from a groin injury suffered during July's Nations Championship. However, Leinster head coach Leo Cullen will be without Byrne and Deegan as they undergo concussion assessments. They join a lengthy casualty list that includes Ireland internationals Caelan Doris, Jordan Larmour and Joey Carbery.

teams.heading: Scotland's former players find no resolution to their massive legal bill
teams.body: There has been no further progress reported today regarding the £2.8 million legal bill hanging over the former Scotland players involved in rugby’s landmark brain injury lawsuit. Since the funding crisis was first detailed last week, no news has emerged of any financial rescue package or settlement talks. The claimants remain in limbo as they seek the resources required to keep their litigation active against the game's governing bodies.

teams.heading: Louis Rees-Zammit scores two tries for Bristol Bears in Wales boost
teams.body: Wales wing Louis Rees-Zammit delivered a commanding performance for Bristol Bears, scoring two tries in a 41-26 victory over Premiership champions Northampton Saints. The 25-year-old's deadly attacking form—including a stunning 50/22 and key defensive plays—comes as a major boost for Steve Tandy ahead of November's Nations Championship. Meanwhile, Dragons hooker Elliot Dee put forward his own international case with a two-try, player-of-the-match display against Scarlets, while young Scarlets wing Macs Page caught the eye as a potential uncapped autumn wildcard.

teams.heading: Argentina launches ambitious joint bid to host 2035 Rugby World Cup
teams.body: Argentina has officially launched a historic four-nation bid alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil to host the men's 2035 Rugby World Cup. The Argentine Rugby Union is leading the proposal, which would bring the tournament to South America for the first time. Technical details have been submitted to World Rugby, listing eight Argentine venues including Buenos Aires' Monumental and José Amalfitani stadiums, alongside Rio de Janeiro’s iconic Maracanã. World Rugby will select the preferred host in May 2027.

teams.heading: Allan Alaalatoa hails 'freak' Mark Nawaqanitawase as winger prepares for rugby return
teams.body: Australia prop Allan Alaalatoa believes the impending return of Mark Nawaqanitawase "automatically lifts the group" ahead of next year's home World Cup. The 26-year-old winger concluded a decorated two-year rugby league stint on Sunday, winning the NRL grand final with the Sydney Roosters. While Nawaqanitawase joins Japan's Saitama Wild Knights in December, Alaalatoa expects his presence to eventually drive internal competition. The Wallabies are currently preparing for a Bledisloe Cup opener against an All Blacks side led by former coach Dave Rennie.

teams.heading: Nel Metcalfe returns to Wales squad for double-header against Japan
teams.body: Full-back Nel Metcalfe has been named in the Wales squad for their upcoming WXV double-header against the Japan Sakura XV. The 21-year-old Gloucester-Hartpury player returns to the international setup following a knee injury that ruled her out of the 2026 Women's Six Nations. Wales are scheduled to face the hosts at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo on 24 October, before the sides meet again seven days later at Kumagaya Rugby Stadium in Saitama Prefecture.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson insists Richie Mo'unga does not own All Blacks fly-half
teams.body: Former All Black Jeff Wilson believes the fly-half jersey remains up for grabs following Ruben Love’s season-ending injury. While Richie Mo'unga is the heavy favourite to start against the Wallabies, Wilson insists the 32-year-old must prove himself, noting that Damian McKenzie remains an option. Assistant coach Jason Ryan confirmed the squad has conducted an honest review of their set-piece struggles, as the team looks to secure a statement performance in the Bledisloe Cup following their recent physical battles against South Africa.

teams.heading: Jason Ryan admits Springboks 'sucked a lot of juice' out All Blacks
teams.body: New Zealand scrum coach Jason Ryan has conceded that the gruelling four-Test series against the Springboks left his squad physically and mentally drained. Reflecting on the 3-1 series defeat, Ryan admitted that the world champions exposed significant vulnerabilities in the All Blacks' set-piece, particularly regarding opposition ball. “The tour sucked a lot of juice out of everyone,” Ryan said. The New Zealand camp is now focused on rectifying these scrum issues ahead of their upcoming Bledisloe Cup matches against Australia.

lead.why: The All Blacks coaching staff have publicly admitted the physical toll and set-piece dominance exerted by the Springboks during their recent series.
